2 Declaration of Commitment The Government of Zambia expresses its strategic intent to develop its metals and minerals sector as a transformative driver of economic growth, job creation, revenue mobilization, and sustainable development. As articulated in Vision 2030, mining is a central pillar in the country’s goal to become a prosperous middle-income nation by 2030. In response to cyclical revenues and the need for economic diversification, the Government has prioritized mining and value addition as a key source of export earnings and economic resilience. Zambia’s mining sector, which produced approximately 890,000 tonnes of copper in 2025, has the potential to increase production significantly towards its target of three (3) million tonnes per year (mtpa) by 2031, with potential to drive a six- to tenfold increase in export revenues over the next decade. Major expansions are already in progress at established operations, including First Quantum’s Kansanshi mine (approximately $1.25 billion CapEx), expanding to 200,000 tonnes per year and Barrick’s Lumwana mine (estimated at $2 billion CapEx), expanding to 240,000 tonnes per year, alongside greenfield prospects like KoBold Metals’ Mingomba property (with an expected CapEx of $2 billion) to produce 300,000 tpa. Under an unconstrained (UC) scenario1, by enacting reforms and pulling policy levers to attract investment and increase production to the three (3) mtpa target, annual revenues could increase to approximately $6.0 billion, a near doubling of the sector’s current fiscal contribution. Commodity Review Copper and Nickel. —In 2024, First Quantum Minerals Ltd. (First Quantum) of Canada was the country's leading copper producer and owned the Enterprise, Kansanshi, and Sentinel Mines. Copper production at the Sentinel Mine was 230,792 metric tons (t) in 2024. The Kansanshi Mine produced 136,007 t of copper concentrates and 34,922 t of copper cathode. Enterprise Mine achieved commercial production status on June 1, 2024, and produced about 19,000 t of nickel by yearend. In 2024, First Quantum advanced its Kansanshi S3 Expansion project, which remained on track for completion in 2025 (First Quantum Minerals Ltd., 2025, p. 3, 14, 76). Barrick Gold Corp. of Canada produced 123,000 t of copper concentrate at the Lumwana Mine in 2024. The company also continued its $2 billion investment in a plant and mine expansion project, which was expected to increase the Lumwana Mine’s production capacity to 240,000 metric tons per year (t/yr) from its current 120,000 - t/yr capacity by 2028. The bankable feasibility study for the expansion project was completed in 2024, with the start of construction projected for 2025 (Facilities table; Barrick Gold Corp., 2025, p. 3, 32, 84).
